purpose: Test whether worked-example supervision yields useful new answers and question-only routing preserves the parent, against a compute-matched control.

architecture.expert: append identity-initialized copies of final two blocks; freeze parent
architecture.control: train original final two blocks; same supervision and actual matched training CPU
architecture.selector: training-only multinomial naive Bayes on question words, equal class priors, Laplace smoothing 1, candidate only when log odds > log(9); otherwise parent
architecture.serving: select once before decoding; one greedy generation; no external arithmetic solver
architecture.head: frozen
architecture.training_execution: verified frozen-prefix cache for training only

data.system: Answer arithmetic questions. For a remainder question, use four lines: First remainder: integer, Second remainder: integer, Sum: integer, Answer: integer. For ordinary addition, reply with only the final integer.

modular-addition: What is the remainder when {a} + {b} is divided by 7?
Add {a} and {b}, then give the remainder after division by seven.
Find the remainder of the sum of {a} and {b} after division by 7.
For {a} plus {b}, what is left over after dividing by seven?
After adding {a} to {b} and dividing the total by 7, which remainder remains?
I need the sum of {a} and {b} modulo seven. What is it?
If {a} plus {b} is divided by seven, how much is left over?
Tell me the remainder for ({a} + {b}) mod 7.
addition: Tell me how much I get from adding {a} to {b}.
I need the total when {a} and {b} are added together.
If I start at {a} and add {b}, what is the result?
Please work out the sum: {a} plus {b}.

data.split: unordered pairs unique across all roles; exclude all six previous arithmetic datasets; evaluation question templates disjoint from training
data.supervision: training modular replies show two operand remainders, their sum and final remainder; evaluation scores complete generated final answer only
data.retention_scope: fresh ordinary arithmetic, not general conversation or previously admitted network windows

training.schedule: six passes over one deterministic shuffled set; no tuning or quality-based early stopping
training.control_stop: first complete step meeting entire expert child CPU bill plus expert-only prefix extension CPU

budget.unit: per-arm CPU and wall seconds; six-hour overall cap; no paid infrastructure
budget.accounting: all children including failures and forced diagnostics billed; common cache and router fit charged once; actual optimization target gives control all expert process overhead

gates.protection: all baseline-correct answers across both evaluation roles; declared before training; never supplied to selector
gates.required_comparisons: served answer beats parent, same-route control and training-majority constant; forced expert must also beat forced control; all paired lower 95% bounds > 0
gates.low_parent_retention: record and finish competence experiment; fewer than four retained correct parent answers fails final protection gate

scope: single-host synthetic arithmetic mechanism only; no network, general assistant, permissionless verification or repeated-growth claim
stop_rule: one committed run; any failed gate stops candidate; no automatic retry, tuning, promotion or follow-up run
